scope: Las Vegas Strip poker tournaments and Strip lodging, built only from official venue and property pages. Snapshot date 2026-11-17. Rows re-read that day carry 2026-11-17 as their last-checked date; every other row keeps the date it was last read.
policy: Every row links the official page it came from. A value that could not be confirmed from an official source is left blank and listed on the Flagged for review page. Walking minutes are Google Maps walking estimates and are labelled as such. The guaranteed-pool-to-fee ratio is descriptive only and is not a forecast.
sessionLengthAssumption: No venue publishes a finish time. The schedule planner assumes a six-hour session plus a 30-minute transfer between venues, so every conflict it reports is an estimate.

single.label: Sheet-screened candidates (entry cap unconfirmed)
single.blurb: The official structure sheet prints one buy-in and no re-entry, rebuy, add-on or second-flight clause, but does not state a maximum number of entries per player. These are candidates only until the venue confirms its written policy.

unverified.label: Unverified — structure sheet not read
unverified.blurb: Published on an official schedule but its structure sheet has not been read, so no entry rule, fee split or chip count is confirmed. These rows keep the unverified label on purpose and are never counted as single-entry events.

flight.label: Multi-flight
flight.blurb: The official schedule publishes separate start flights. A player who does not bag for Day 2 may buy into another flight, so more than one entry is possible.

satellite.label: Satellite (seat prizes, not cash)
satellite.blurb: Prizes are entries into another event, not cash. Different maths: see the ratio note.

bounty.label: Bounty / PKO
bounty.blurb: Part of the guarantee is paid as bounties, so the printed guarantee is not a cash prize pool.

extra.label: Extra-spend formats (re-entry, rebuy, add-on, paid chip boost)
extra.blurb: Isolated from the single-entry list. Each format gives a way to spend more than the printed buy-in.

special.label: Restricted or team format
special.blurb: Team, female-only or age-restricted formats. They are labelled so they are never mistaken for an open single-entry event.

wpt.label: Wynn tournament series
wpt.blurb: Rows from the official WPT World Championship and Wynn Signature Series schedule PDFs.

recurring.label: Recurring daily or weekly room tournaments
recurring.blurb: A published cadence rather than a dated event.

conflict.label: Source conflict (not ranked)
conflict.blurb: The official sources disagree, so the monetary fields are left blank.

hotels.name: The Venetian Resort (poker suite rate)
hotels.rooms: Luxury King Suite, single or double occupancy
hotels.baseRateNote: The official poker-room rate page states: 'These rates will start as low as $119 and $209 and can be higher.' The page does not map each starting figure to a specific property and no date-specific quote is published.
hotels.resortFeeNote: $55 resort fee per night stayed, plus tax, payable upon check-in.
hotels.taxNote: Printed in the official Hotel Terms and Conditions, 'Taxes, Surcharges, and Resort Fee' section: 'Daily rates do not include the applicable Clark County Room Tax of 13.38%.' The county per-property schedule prints the same 13.38% for a resort hotel in the Primary Gaming Corridor, and the resort fee is 'plus applicable tax' per night. The same terms page still opens its Resort Fee section with 'Rates include a daily Resort Fee of $55 plus tax per night', and the booking calendar footnote says its prices 'include daily resort fee, excludes taxes', so two official pages describe the fee differently and the site uses the fee-on-top reading (F51).
hotels.parking: $20 per day for registered hotel guests (seven days a week); $20 Monday-Thursday and $25 Friday-Sunday for non-hotel guests; valet $40 per day (hotel terms). The resort's own poker-room parking page repeats those figures and adds a waiver: 'Players in the poker room who play three hours or more in tournament or cash games will receive complimentary self-parking for the day.' Venetian Rewards Sapphire and above park free; Nevada residents get three hours free; event parking rates may be in effect and rates are 'subject to change'.

parkingWaiver.excerpt: Players in the poker room who play three hours or more in tournament or cash games will receive complimentary self-parking for the day. Players must visit a supervisor at the end of their session to confirm qualifications for complimentary self-parking.
parkingWaiver.conditions: Validated by a supervisor at the end of the session. The same page adds, in its own words, that 'Venetian Rewards Sapphire members and above receive complimentary self-parking' and that 'Event parking rates may be in effect and are subject to change; check posted signage for additional details.' It also gives Nevada residents three hours of complimentary self-parking by scanning a valid Nevada driver's licence at a self-parking kiosk, not available while event parking rates are in effect; that clause is paraphrased because the page's own punctuation could not be reproduced byte for byte in this capture.
parkingWaiver.tierRoute: 75 cash-game hours or 15 tournaments in the past 12 months can be emailed to the address on the page to be validated for Sapphire tier, which carries complimentary self-parking.
parkingWaiver.whyNotApplied: The $20 per night stays in every published total. No official source publishes a tournament finish time (F16), so a three-hour session cannot be confirmed for a named event, and the page makes the waiver conditional on a supervisor confirming the session. The waiver is published beside the figure, not folded into it.

hotels.cancellation: A deposit for the stay including suite, fee and tax is billed on reservation confirmation. Blackout dates apply. Prepaid offers are non-cancellable and non-refundable. Early checkout before the scheduled departure date costs $100 plus tax.
hotels.incidental: $150 per night credit card incidental deposit for suite charging privileges (non-Signature Suites).
hotels.checkInOut: Check-in 3:00 PM to 11:59 PM; check-out 11:00 AM.
hotels.qualification: Poker-suite rates require six hours of active live cash play, or a buy-in to a $300 or higher tournament, for each night stayed, completed before 2 a.m. on the last night. Book with code EPOKR25 on 866.255.8936. Failure to qualify means the prevailing rate is charged.

flags.title: The official WPT schedule PDF labels December 18 as both a Wednesday and a Friday
flags.detail: In the same PDF, 'Dec. 18 Wednesday' carries the No Limit Hold'em Day 1A and PLO rows while 'Dec. 18 Friday' carries the WPT World Championship Day 4 rows. The rows also run out of order, with the December 17 block printed after the December 18 Wednesday block, and no December 16 block appears anywhere in the PDF. December 18, 2026 is a Friday. Flag F61 sets out the official evidence that the day number, not the weekday, is the misprint and that these eight rows are very likely December 16. The schedule dates are reproduced exactly as printed and the dispute is flagged rather than corrected, because the site does not silently re-date a row on an inference.

flags.title: Bellagio Saturday buy-in is printed three different ways on official sources
flags.detail: The poker-room page links the event as 'SATURDAYS | $1,000 NLH'; the structure PDF header reads 'NLH $1100 BUY-IN'; rule 07 of the same PDF reads 'Of the $600 Buy-in, $510 goes to the Prize Pool, $50 is Admin Fees and $40 is optional staff gratuity'. The row is therefore left blank for buy-in and guarantee and is not ranked.

flags.title: Bellagio tournament-resumption notice is undated and names July 26
flags.detail: The poker page still carries the notice 'Tournament play will resume on Saturday, July 26, beginning with the $300 PLO Double Board Bomb Pot Tournament at 2 PM PT.' No year is printed, July 26, 2026 was a Sunday, and the page highlights elsewhere say the PLO Double Bomb Pot runs nightly at 6 PM. The start time is therefore left as the page highlight value and the notice is listed as a conflict.

flags.title: Venetian NYE schedule prints 'Saturday, December 26, 2025' for three events
flags.detail: Events 5, 6 and 7 of the DeepStack Extravaganza NYE page are dated 'Saturday, December 26, 2025' even though the series runs December 24, 2026 to January 10, 2027. The page also misspells 'Tuesaday'. The rows are kept at 2026-12-26 and the printed label is flagged here.

flags.title: Structure sheet 13 cross-references the wrong companion sheet
flags.detail: Sheet 12 covers 'Day A+C+E' and points to 'SEE OTHER STRUCTURE SHEET FOR DAYS B+D+F'. Sheet 13 covers 'Day B+D' but points to 'SEE OTHER STRUCTURE SHEET FOR DAYS A+C+F', which should read A+C+E. Sheet 14 covers Day F and points to A+B+C+D+E. The flight groups themselves agree with the schedule page; only the cross-reference is wrong.

flags.title: Two NYE events are labelled (1Day) but have a Day 2 restart on the same schedule page
flags.detail: Event 27 '$250 No Limit Hold'em 1A $75K GTD (1Day)' carries the note 'Day 1 Payouts with 5% advancing to Day 2' and a Day 2 Restart on January 6, 2027. Event 30 '$300 No Limit Hold'em 1A $100K GTD (1Day)' has a Day 2 Restart on January 10, 2027. Both are treated as multi-day.

flags.title: MGM Grand weekly schedule sheet is headed 'August Tournament Schedule'
flags.detail: The PDF linked from the MGM Grand poker-room page is titled 'MGM Grand August Tournament Schedule' while the room page itself is current. The daily slots and buy-ins are used as printed; the month label is flagged.

flags.title: MGM Grand $120 payout table does not line up with its own entry ranges
flags.detail: Rows such as '71-77' list eleven payout percentages and '64-70' list ten, which cannot both describe a seven-entry range. The payout table is not used for any comparison on this site.

flags.title: The MGM Grand $120 structure PDF carries the title 'Max Stacks Tournament Series'
flags.detail: The document title on the PDF is 'Max Stacks Tournament Series' although its content is the $120 No Limit Hold'em structure. Content matches the poker-room page; the title does not.

flags.title: LIPS flat-fee wording on sheets 31, 32 and 33 is ambiguous
flags.detail: Sheet 33 reads '$80 of the $600 Buy-In is withheld for house fees (Rake + Staff). $10 of the $600 Buy In will be withheld as a flat fee for ... Ladies International Poker Series (LIPS). Prize pool consists of $510 of every $600 Buy In.' Read as two separate withholdings ($80 + $10 + $510) the total is $600; read as one, it is $590. The figures are reported as printed with the ambiguity flagged.

flags.title: The NYE series is fully read, but three of its sheets print multi-entry wording the schedule page omits
flags.detail: Resolved on 2026-11-17: the 15 DeepStack Extravaganza NYE structure sheets were read in full, so no NYE row is marked 'structure sheet not read'. The sheets change the picture that the schedule page alone gives. Sheet 2 ($200 Bounty) and sheet 9 ($200 Valuetown Bounty) both print a 'subsequent re-entry' sentence, and sheet 15's $250 flight series says a player 'may play another flight', so those rows are multi-entry and stay out of the single-entry path. Sheets 1, 3, 10, 11 and 12 print no re-entry, rebuy or add-on clause and are recorded as single entry on the sheet. Sheets 6, 8, 13 and 14 print bagging clauses and are counted as multi-flight. The remaining sheets are satellites or bounty events with their own wording, quoted on each row.

flags.title: Thirteen WPT events now carry their printed rules; the $10,400 World Championship and the satellites still have no published section
flags.detail: The official structures PDF was read end to end on 2026-11-17 (all eight chunks) and every event section it publishes is transcribed in raw/wynn_wpt_world_championship_structures_2026-11-17.md. Thirty-five schedule rows now match a section on date, start slot, buy-in and printed name: the $600 NLH $400K flights (Nov 27-29), the $800 NLH $1M flights (Nov 30-Dec 2), the $1,600 NLH $1M flights (Dec 3-4), the $1,100 WPT Prime flights (Dec 5-8), the $1,600 PLO Mystery Bounty flights (Dec 6), and the single-day TORSE, PLO, Mixed Triple Draw, Limit Omaha 8, Limit Omaha 8/Stud 8, $1,100 PLO, HORSE and $600 NLH Turbo events. Every one of those sections prints re-entry, so none of them is a single-entry event, and none prints an add-on or rebuy provision. What remains unverified is listed here rather than implied: the $10,400 WPT World Championship has no section at all; the Dec 18 $3,000 and $10,500 events, the Super Gold Million Mystery Bounty, the Seniors and Ladies championships, the NLH Mystery Bounty, the Wynn Mixed Championship, the TORSE and Limit Omaha 8 championships and every Milestone Satellite have no section either. Day 2 and final-table rows keep 'not-verified' because the document publishes entry rules for starting flights, not for restarts, and two of them (Nov 30 1 p.m. and Dec 3 1 p.m.) carry the following event's buy-in columns in the schedule PDF (F34).

flags.title: The ARIA poker guide is undated and the current page asks guests to confirm by phone
flags.detail: The official guide states daily 1 PM and nightly 7 PM events but carries no date. The current poker page asks guests to call or check @ARIAPoker for whether daily events are running, and publishes no buy-in, guarantee or entry rules. The rows are kept as an undated cadence only.

flags.title: Wynn resort fee differs between published offer pages
flags.detail: The general Wynn terms used here state 'A daily resort fee of $55 plus tax'. An older, expired offer page states $50 plus tax. The actual fee on a booked reservation controls; $55 plus tax is used and the discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved.

flags.title: RESOLVED 2026-11-17: a dated checkout total exists for the booked trip window ($4,010.55, 23-30 Nov 2026)
flags.detail: Superseded on the evening of 2026-11-17; the record is kept because it is the largest money gap the dashboard carried. The booking engine printed an itemised total for the stay the trip is actually booked for: 23-30 November 2026, seven nights, two adults, Newly Remodeled Luxury King under 'Book Direct: Up to 25% Off', $4,010.55 with $473.30 of tax and nightly room rates of $164.25, $164.25, $201.75, $231.75, $1,649.25, $554.25 and $186.75 before a $55 resort fee each night. Every night reconciles to (rate + $55) x 1.1338 and the seven derived figures add to the printed total exactly. The trip cost model now uses that total and publishes the $197.28 component floor beside it. For completeness on the superseded dates: four stay windows inside the then-recommended 25 November - 2 December 2026 returned no suite and no price, and two earlier near-term stays are still in the rate log as observations (17-19 November at $1,245.48 on 2026-11-16 and $1,015.89 on 2026-11-17, 20-22 November at $2,504.00). What remains open is narrower and is carried by F66: the phone-only poker rate (code EPOKR25) does not appear in the engine quote.

flags.title: The Venetian booking calendar disagrees with the quote, and its cells change with the query
flags.detail: The calendar cell for November 17 read $855 in the observation recorded on 2026-11-16, while the same page's quote for the same night printed a $824.25 room rate, and an earlier observation of the same calendar on the same day recorded $605. The calendar states that its prices are the best available suite and rate, include the daily resort fee and exclude taxes. Calendar cells are logged as observations and are never used in a total. On 2026-11-17 the same booking engine was fetched live for the superseded 25 November - 2 December window and showed no amount in any date cell; the engine was then opened for the booked 23-30 November stay and printed an itemised $4,010.55 total (F15), while its calendar cells for those nights were still different figures (F69). No calendar cell is ever recorded as a price.

flags.title: The official schedule PDF and the official schedule page print the event name differently
flags.detail: Both captures are official and they agree on date, time, event number and structure-sheet link for all 94 rows, but 83 of the 94 names are rendered differently: the PDF puts the guarantee in its own GUARANTEE column, while the HTML page inlines '$XXK GTD' into the event name. Example: the PDF prints '$200 NLH BOUNTY (1DAY)' with a separate $8,000 guarantee, and the page prints '$200 No Limit Hold'em Bounty $8K GTD (1Day)'. The site's names follow the HTML page, which is the page every row links to.

flags.title: The official schedule PDF prints decorative sponsor art in the DATE column on 20 rows
flags.detail: 20 of the 94 rows on the official DeepStack Extravaganza IV schedule PDF carry no date at all: 6 read '@PokerAtlas* TOUR', 6 read 'LIPS CHAMPIONSHIP CHAMPIES CHAMPIES CHAMPIES', 5 read 'LIPS FRIDAY, DECEMBER 11', 2 read '@PokerAtlas PRO' and 1 reads '@PokerAtlas* PRO'. Those rows cover events 17, 18, 32-38, 41-46, 48, 50, 51 and 58. The dates on this site for those rows come from the official schedule page, not from the PDF, and the two were cross-checked row by row.

flags.title: Booking-calendar cells are not prices: the same date prints a different figure per query
flags.detail: On 2026-11-17 the official Venetian booking calendar was read twice, with two different stay windows open. November 16 printed $555 with the November 17-19 window open and $854 with the November 27-28 window open; November 22 printed $165 against $230; November 27 printed $905 against $1,814. The page's own footnote says the figure is the best available suite and rate, includes the daily resort fee and excludes taxes, so the cell tracks the cheapest suite the engine can offer for that context rather than a fixed nightly rate. No calendar cell is used anywhere on this site as a price; only the engine's itemised quote panel is.

flags.title: No official schedule publishes tournament finish times
flags.detail: Venetian sheets publish start time, level length and late-registration cut-off but no finish time. The overlap check therefore uses a stated planning assumption (a six-hour session plus a 30-minute transfer between venues) and every conflict it reports is an estimate, not an official statement.

flags.title: The earliest verified official start is 9:00 AM (Horseshoe daily); no 8:00 AM start is published
flags.detail: Re-read on 2026-11-17 on the Caesars page: Horseshoe runs six daily No-Limit Hold'em games at 9 a.m., 11 a.m., 2 p.m., 5 p.m., 8 p.m. and 11 p.m., with no buy-in published. Caesars Palace runs four daily games at 10 a.m., 2 p.m., 6 p.m. and 9 p.m. (the official flyer prints $100 buy-ins at 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. and $160 at 2 p.m. and 9 p.m., with an optional $50 add-on; read 2026-11-18, F90). On the Venetian schedule re-read on 2026-11-17 the earliest start is 9:10 AM, a $260 satellite on Dec 12. Re-read live on 2026-11-19 from the official DSE IV schedule page (all four chunks): the 9:10 AM row is Saturday, December 12, Event 46; the two 10:00 AM Venetian rows are Friday, December 11 (Event 39, Day 2 Restart) and Tuesday, December 15 (Event 49, Day 2 Restart); the earliest opening event is 10:10 AM. Opening Venetian events start at 10:10 AM or later; the only 10:00 AM Venetian starts are restarts (Day 2 or Day 3). Inside the 23-29 November trip window no opening event starts before 11:10 AM; the only earlier start there is the Day 2 restart at 11:00 AM on 25 November (read 2026-11-19). The Wynn daily starts at 12:00 PM. Most Wynn WPT rows start at 11:00 AM. Its 10:00 AM rows are the Super Gold Million flights (Dec 10 and 11), one WPT row on Dec 12 and a satellite on Dec 18, all from the WPT PDF read on 2026-11-16. An 'all day from 8:00 AM' plan cannot be built from official sources. The day plan starts at the earliest verified start for each venue.

flags.title: Wynn daily tournaments are suspended during Wynn Signature, Wynn Millions and Classic series
flags.detail: Stated on the official poker-room page. It matters for date selection: the daily $200 and $160 events cannot be assumed to run during those windows.

flags.title: Hotel cost comparison is limited to published per-night components
flags.detail: No reviewed property publishes parking cost inside the room folio, incidentals, or the tax rate as a single checkout total, so the like-for-like comparison is built from the same published components for every property: room rate, mandatory resort fee, tax, parking and cancellation deadline.

flags.title: Horseshoe daily buy-ins, levels and guarantees are not published
flags.detail: The official Caesars page publishes six Horseshoe start times but states only that 'a mixture of buy-ins, levels and guarantees caters to all participants'. Every Horseshoe monetary field is therefore blank.

flags.title: Google Maps resolved 'Horseshoe Las Vegas' to Bally's on the first query
flags.detail: The first walking query using the property name alone was routed from Bally's Las Vegas. The figure shown for Horseshoe was re-taken using the full street address and the result is labelled as such. Walking times are Google Maps estimates captured on 2026-11-16, not venue-published figures.

flags.title: Several schedule rows on the Wynn Signature Series PDF carry an extra empty cell
flags.detail: The rows for '1/17 NLH TURBO', '1/18 NO LIMIT HOLD'EM DAY 1A' and '1/18 NLH TURBO' have one more cell than the table header, which shifts the guarantee column: the printed guarantee appears in the entry column and the entry price appears in the chip column. The values are read in the order the surrounding rows use, so the $10,000 and $100,000 figures are treated as the guarantee and $200 or $400 as the entry. The guarantee for the milestone satellites is printed as '10 Seats'. Re-read on 2026-11-17: the shift is still on the page, and the same pattern also moves the guarantee out of its column on the 1/17 1 P.M. Day 2, 1/18 PLO, 1/19 TORSE, 1/20 MIXED TRIPLE DRAW, 1/21 TOE, 1/22 BIG O and 1/24 PLO DOUBLE BOARD BOMB POT rows, which print no guarantee cell. Those rows are shown with a blank guarantee rather than a shifted figure.

flags.title: The official DSE schedule page misspells 'Limit' on four rows
flags.detail: The schedule page prints 'No LImit Hold'em' with a capital letter i on the rows for event 2 (November 18), event 6 (November 22), event 10 (November 25) and event 12 (November 26). The event names on this site use the corrected spelling and every row links the page and the structure sheet, so the printed label can be checked in one click.

flags.title: The Ladies Championship entry fee is printed twice, differently
flags.detail: The WPT schedule prints the buy-in column as '$1,100' for 'Ladies NIH Championship (2 Day)' while the footnote under the table reads 'The Tournament Entry for the Ladies Championship is $11,100. Ladies will receive a discounted entry.' The event name is printed as 'NIH', which is a typo for No Limit Hold'em. The row keeps the printed column value and the footnote is recorded with it; nothing is adjusted.

flags.title: The '$1,000,000 Added' on the WPT World Championship is not available in Nevada
flags.detail: The schedule prints 'WPT World Championship Day 1A $1,000,000 Added' for $10,400, and the footnote under the table states: '$1,000,000 will be added in cash prizes by ClubWPT Gold. ClubWPT Gold is not available in Nevada.' The guarantee column for those rows is blank on the schedule. A Nevada player therefore cannot count the added million, which is why no guarantee is shown for those rows.

flags.title: The five footnote markers on the WPT schedule PDF: what each one says, and the four **** rows it does not describe
flags.detail: Re-read with the whole schedule PDF on 2026-11-17 (both chunks) so the resolution is recorded rather than called unclear. The markers, in the PDF's own order, read: (1) '*' - 'Winners will receive two (2) prizes valued at $1,100 each. Prizes may be used separately or combined for a tournament entry.'; (2) '**' - 'Winners will receive direct entry to the corresponding event(s) for which it was held.'; (3) '***' - '$1,000,000 will be added in cash prizes by ClubWPT Gold. ClubWPT Gold is not available in Nevada.'; (4) '****' - 'The Tournament Entry for the Ladies Championship is $11,100. Ladies will receive a discounted entry.'; (5) '*****' - 'Players registered prior to the start of the event will receive a discounted entry.'. Markers 1, 2, 3 and 5 are printed on rows the text describes and are carried with those rows. Marker 4 is the unresolved one. The footnote describes one event - the Ladies Championship, printed as 'Ladies NIH Championship' at $1,100 on Dec 13 - and the PDF prints the marker on seven rows in total: that row plus six the footnote does not describe (PLO 6-Max $10,500, the Milestone Satellite to the $25K NLH High Roller $3,000, the NLH High Roller $25,800, NLH 6-Max $10,500, PLO $10,500 and NLH 8-Max $10,500). Nothing is adjusted on any of them and none is treated as discounted; the printed buy-in is shown. If the marker means the same thing on all seven rows then the six high-roller-style prices are not the amount payable and the site overstates them, which is why this stays open rather than resolved. Marker 5 appears on no captured row. Confirm with the Wynn poker room (702.770.7654, printed on the same PDF).

flags.title: The RaceDay Stack sheets print no guarantee
flags.detail: Sheets 18 and 29 print the buy-in, rake and blind structure but no guarantee line, so events 3, 4, 5 and 6 carry a blank guarantee and are not ranked by the guaranteed-pool-to-fee ratio.

flags.title: The site root served a stale page that contradicted the dashboard, because two publishers wrote to the same URL
flags.detail: GitHub Pages was configured to deploy from the main branch root while pages.yml also deployed the site/ artifact, so the URL /Poker3/ served whichever deployment finished last. At the time this was found the root served an earlier-round page (46 Venetian rows, no verified hotel cost, 'no hotel ranking is shown'), while /Poker3/site/ served the canonical 341-row dashboard. A visitor landing on the site root therefore saw conclusions the live data contradicts. The root page is now a redirect and pages.yml redeploys after the branch build; the underlying setting (Pages source = 'deploy from a branch') could not be changed by this session's token, which is why the redirect exists as a second guarantee.

flags.title: No scheduled source re-check had produced a run yet, and the three monitors were not serialised against each other
flags.detail: At inspection time no run of checks.yml, monitor.yml or daily-check.yml existed, and site/checks.json, which the sources page fetches, did not exist either, so the page reported 'No automated check file yet'. The reason for the zero runs is timing, not deletion: all three workflows reached main at 00:44 UTC on 2026-11-17 and their crons were 12:13, 12:05 and 09:00 UTC, so the first scheduled time had not arrived. The real defect is that monitor.yml and daily-check.yml had no concurrency group at all while checks.yml used its own, so they could have collided once the crons fired; daily-check.yml additionally rewrote the tree and force-rebased onto main, and monitor.yml pushed with '|| true', which hides a rejected push. They are now one serialised job with a rebase-retry push. It is registered and active; its first run is the 12:13 UTC cron, and this page does not claim a run has been observed.

flags.title: The structure sheets do not confirm a one-entry-per-player maximum
flags.detail: The 52 Venetian rows classified as 'single entry on the sheet' have one printed buy-in and no re-entry, rebuy, add-on or second-flight provision in the reviewed sheet. However, the sheets do not state a maximum number of entries per player and do not explicitly call the event a freezeout. This is only a document-level screen, not written confirmation of the room's one-entry policy. Do not treat these candidates as strictly eligible or book around them until the venue confirms the maximum-entry, no-rebuy and no-add-on rules in writing. The source excerpt and date are attached to each row. Re-read 2026-11-19: the live official DSE IV schedule (all four chunks) prints no 'one entry', 'freezeout' or re-entry label on any row; its only entry wording is 'Direct Entry to Event #47 / #39' (satellites) and rake-discount notes. The venue does print one-entry wording on schedule rows in other series: the official DeepStack Extravaganza II page (April 2023, dse-apr-2023.html) prints 'One Entry Only with One Hour of Registration' on Event 13 (read live 2026-11-19). So the venue's schedule vocabulary includes a one-entry label, and the 2026 series prints none on any row. That is still not a written maximum-entry rule for the 2026 series, so F31 remains open. The question to put to the venue is in research/reread_2026-11-19.md.

flags.title: Eight WPT rows are probably two days late: the 'Dec. 18 Wednesday' block is very likely December 16
flags.detail: The official WPT schedule PDF prints one block labelled 'Dec. 18 Wednesday' and a second labelled 'Dec. 18 Friday' holding different events, and it prints no December 16 block at all. Four pieces of official evidence say the Wednesday block is December 16. (1) It sits between the December 15 Tuesday block and the December 17 Thursday block in print order, exactly where December 16 belongs. (2) December 16, 2026 is a Wednesday, which is the weekday the block prints. (3) It carries WPT World Championship Day 2, and that event's Day 1C is printed on December 15 while its Day 3 is printed on December 17, so Day 2 has to fall between them. (4) The $1,100 No Limit Hold'em whose Day 1A and Day 1B appear in the block has its 'No Limit Hold'em Day 2' printed inside the December 17 block. The day number therefore looks like the misprint, not the weekday. The site keeps the date exactly as printed, because re-dating a row on an inference is exactly what this project promises not to do, so these eight rows remain dated 2026-12-18: that collides them with the genuine December 18 rows and leaves 2026-12-16 empty. Confirm against the room's own published calendar before planning around any of them. Flag F01 recorded the PDF's self-contradiction and concluded the weekday was the error; this flag records the evidence that reverses that conclusion, and F01 has been amended to point here.

flags.title: Four WPT event names read differently from the printed text
flags.detail: The schedule PDF prints 'NIH Turbo', 'NIH $500 Bounty Turbo' and 'Milestone Satellite to $25K NIH High Roller', and it prints 'Double Play Milestone Satellite1' with a trailing digit. The published rows read 'NLH Turbo', 'NLH $500 Bounty Turbo', 'Milestone Satellite to $25K NLH High Roller' and 'Double Play Milestone Satellite'. NIH is almost certainly the PDF's own rendering of NLH, but NIH is what is printed, so this is a normalisation rather than a transcription and it is recorded as one. Every other cell on those four rows - date, start time, buy-in, guarantee, chips and level length - was re-checked against the PDF on 2026-11-17 and agrees.

flags.title: Day 2 restart rows carry values that their own schedule row leaves blank
flags.detail: The official DeepStack Extravaganza IV series schedule PDF prints an empty GUARANTEE, CHIPS, LEVEL and REG CLOSES cell for every Day 2 restart row, because those rows continue an event whose Day 1 row already printed them. The published restart rows fill those cells with the values printed on that event's own structure sheet, so the figures are official but they come from the sheet, not from the restart row. A line-by-line re-check of all 94 rows against the PDF on 2026-11-17 found 43 such cells, all on Day 2 restart rows, and no other disagreement anywhere in the series.

flags.title: Two different official booking requests gave two different answers for the trip window
flags.detail: Asking the official Venetian booking engine for the trip window itself (arrival 2026-11-25, departure 2026-12-02) returned $XXX in every cell on the earlier read, so no checkout total was obtained for those nights; a later read of 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-30 did return one ($4,010.55, F36). Asking the same engine for a calendar view (arrival 2026-11-17) prints per-night cells for 17-30 November, including $185 on 25 November, $190 on 26 November, $210 on 27 November, $905 on 28 November, $340 on 29 November and $165 on 30 November, and the calendar states those cells include the daily resort fee and exclude taxes. A note carried by an earlier build of this site said the trip window published no price at all, which those cells contradict; a later live re-read rewrote that note, and this flag keeps the two requests distinct so the claim cannot return. The calendar cells are still not a quote, and nothing here converts them into one: they are recorded so a reader can see that part of the window does have published figures.

flags.title: Printed Venetian tax for the 23-30 Nov quote is $0.02 above 13.38% of its pre-tax subtotal
flags.detail: Dated official booking-engine read on 2026-11-17 (2 adults, 23-30 Nov 2026, 7 nights): the printed nightly rates total $3,152.25, the printed resort fees total $385.00, the pre-tax subtotal is $3,537.25, and the printed tax is $473.30. 13.38% of $3,537.25 is $473.28. The page does not explain the $0.02 difference. The record keeps the printed $473.30 and the printed $4,010.55 total, and does not adjust either figure. Per-night true costs are derived as (rate + $55) x 1.1338 and sum to the printed total.

flags.title: Walking-route estimates are point-in-time Google Maps readings
flags.detail: The hotel-by-venue matrix now holds all 56 pairs (8 hotel records × 7 venue records): 14 rows from the 2026-11-16 base pass plus 42 rows read on 2026-11-17 — 41 resort-to-resort readings added by that pass and the Venetian-to-Bellagio row added by a concurrent pass with poker-room endpoints (27 min, see F67). Cross-checks: every resort-to-resort pair measured agrees with its already-published reverse direction within one minute, except Wynn-venue rows, where the new pass walked to Encore (where the poker room actually is) while the stored wynn-origin rows start at Wynn Las Vegas. What remains flagged: every figure is a reading of one moment — sidewalks, crossings and route recommendations change — endpoint choice alone moves the answer by several minutes (F67), and no unofficial path is used. Re-measure the specific pair on Google or Apple Maps before relying on it, and confirm the official property addresses. The tournament table's 30-minute limit is opt-in, not a default, so it cannot hide rows before the reader asks; it is measured from the hotel the reader selects, and a pair resolved only by the reverse of a recorded row is labelled 'reverse of the recorded pair', because a reversed row is a property-to-property figure whose far end is the resort address rather than the poker room.

flags.title: The dated Venetian checkout total rests on one successful engine read; a second read the same evening returned no prices
flags.detail: The $4,010.55 all-in total for 23-30 November 2026 was printed by the official booking engine on 2026-11-17 and re-read that evening at 21:5x UTC (see F15). A third read from this session at 22:33 UTC on the same URL returned no price at all: every calendar cell rendered the placeholder '$XXX', the suite panel showed only 'Your Venice meets Vegas getaway is loading', and no checkout summary was returned. That is the same rendering failure this repository recorded for four other stay windows, so it is treated as evidence that the engine does not serve a stable static price to every reader, not as evidence that the price moved. F78, published by a concurrent session, records a different failure of the same engine on the same night: the same trip-window query returned two different suites and totals about 20 minutes apart. Read the two together - the engine is not a stable source for a static reader. Consequence for a decision: the published total is dated, reproducible from the recorded nightly figures and internally consistent (every night reconciles to (rate + $55) x 1.1338 and the seven figures add to the printed total), but it must be re-read at the moment of booking before any non-refundable payment. Nothing on the site was revalued on the strength of the failed read.

flags.title: Sources re-read on 2026-11-17 (22:3x UTC) that match the published rows, recorded so the re-check date is not lost
flags.detail: Re-read line by line from this session with no change found, and therefore no value edited: the Venetian DeepStack IV schedule page (chunk 0 of 4, 16-28 November rows: event numbers, dates, start times, buy-ins, guarantees and structure-sheet links all agree with site/data.json); the Venetian 2026 poker suite-rates page ('rates will start as low as $119 and $209', '$55 resort fee per night stayed', the six-hours-cash-or-$300-tournament qualification, code EPOKR25, the 150-day horizon); the Wynn WPT World Championship structures PDF (chunks 0, 1, 4 and 5 of 8: the general terms, and the $600 NLH, $600 Limit Omaha 8/Stud 8, $1,100 PLO, $1,600 NLH, $600 HORSE and $1,100 Prime Championship sections, each fee split, registration clause and starting stack quoting exactly as published, including the $1,100 section whose components add to $1,105 - F60); the Wynn resort policies page ('a daily resort fee of $55 plus tax', check-in 3 p.m., check-out 12 p.m., self-parking for up to two vehicles included in the fee); the Bellagio terms and conditions ('A daily resort fee of $55.00 plus applicable tax', $50 plus tax per additional occupant, 72-hour cancellation window, $150 per day incidental authorisation); and the Caesars Palace booking page ('$62.30 ($54.95 plus $7.35 tax)', 'Rates shown reflect the lowest available rate and include applicable resort fees'). Caesars' printed fee-plus-tax figures divide to 13.375%, and Horseshoe's ($49.95 plus $6.68) to 13.373%, which corroborates the 13.38% Clark County room tax used by the cost model from the properties' own pages rather than only from the Venetian's terms.

flags.title: Day 2 restarts of earlier Venetian events overlap the trip-window primaries
flags.detail: Re-read on 2026-11-17 from the official schedule: Event #7 ($400 No Limit Hold'em flights) has a Day 2 Restart at 11:00 AM on Wed Nov 25, the same morning as the 11:10 AM primary (#10). Event #19 ($400 flights) has a Day 2 Restart at 11:00 AM on Wed Dec 2, and its 11:10 AM Day 1 flight on Sun Nov 29 is the same morning as the 12:10 PM primary (#20). A restart applies only to a player who bagged chips in an earlier flight, so the day plan treats these as conditional and does not model them. Before relying on a primary, check whether any earlier flight was played.

flags.title: The WPT schedule and the WPT structure PDF give different dates for the same events
flags.detail: Read on 2026-11-17. The schedule PDF lists a 'No Limit Hold'em Day 2' for the $800 NLH on Mon Nov 30 at 1:00 PM, but the structure PDF gives that event Day 1A at 11 a.m. on Mon Nov 30 and Day 2 at 1 p.m. on Thu Dec 3. The schedule also lists a 'No Limit Hold'em (2 Day)' $1,600 on Dec 9 at 11 a.m., while the structure PDF gives the $1,600 NLH Day 1A on Thu Dec 3 and Day 2 on Sat Dec 5. The rows are reproduced as printed and not corrected. The $800 row is not matched to a structure section for that reason. Confirm the date with the poker room before any decision that depends on it.

flags.title: The Wynn terms page cited for the resort fee is an expired 2025 offer; the cancellation term lives elsewhere
flags.detail: The earlier build cited https://www.wynnlasvegas.com/terms-and-conditions/850070 for Wynn's $55 resort fee, parking and 48-hour cancellation. That page is a DINING CREDIT offer whose own text says a stay booked under it 'must be completed on or before September 30, 2025', so it cannot substantiate a November 2026 trip. The fee was re-verified on 2026-11-17 from the live Resort Policies page, which still prints $55 plus tax, check-in 3 p.m. and check-out 12 p.m.; that page does not print a cancellation window. Corrected 2026-11-17 on a second live read: the 48-hour window is NOT confined to offer terms. The live Terms page (the same /terms-and-conditions/850070 URL) carries a 'CANCELLATION POLICY' section whose body reads 'cancellations must be received at least 48 hours prior to arrival date or deposit (if applicable) will be forfeited', plus an early-departure penalty of the departing night's rate and tax. The hotel row now records that general 48-hour term with the Terms URL as its source, and notes that the same page also prints offer-specific date exceptions that were not read one by one.

flags.title: RESOLVED 2026-11-17: the booking engine does print an itemised total for the trip window; the $XXX cells were a rendering artefact
flags.detail: Superseded on the evening of 2026-11-17. This flag was written against the superseded 25 November - 2 December window, where the date picker returned every cell reading $XXX because prices load by script after first paint, so no dated total could be read for those dates. Reopening the engine for the window the trip is booked for (23-30 November 2026) returned the itemised panel and the $4,010.55 checkout total described in F15. The lesson is kept on the register rather than deleted: the calendar cells and the itemised panel can disagree, so no calendar cell is ever used as a price (F69). The published starting-rate floor ($197.28) is still shown beside the quote and is still labelled a floor, never a quote.

flags.title: Caesars Palace and Horseshoe resort fees are now confirmed; their room-tax percentage is not
flags.detail: Closed on 2026-11-17 for the fee. The official Caesars booking page for each property prints a Hotel Policies > Fees block: Caesars Palace 'Resort fees: $62.30 ($54.95 plus $7.35 tax)' with a '$100 per day' deposit, and Horseshoe Las Vegas 'Resort fees: $56.63 ($49.95 plus $6.68 tax)' with a '$50 per day' deposit, a $75 pet fee and a $30-per-day rollaway. Both pages add that 'Rates shown reflect the lowest available rate and include applicable resort fees' and that the fee is not assessed for Diamond and Seven Stars guests. What remains open: neither page prints a room-tax percentage for the rate, and neither publishes a self-parking amount, so a true nightly cost is still not computed from property-published components. The third-party spread that blocked this row earlier ($42, $49.95, $54.95, $55, $62.30) is resolved: the $54.95/$49.95 figures are the pre-tax fees and the $62.30/$56.63 figures are the same fees with tax.

flags.title: Room-tax % is still blank in the property-published column for Wynn, Caesars, Horseshoe, Bellagio, MGM Grand and ARIA; a county per-property reference now sits beside each
flags.detail: Checked 2026-11-17 (session arena/5b8ce14d-poker3). No property page read this session prints a room-tax percentage for its room rate. Wynn's terms page prints a $55 resort fee 'plus tax' with no percentage. Caesars and Horseshoe print only the tax amount on their resort fee ($7.35 on $54.95; $6.68 on $49.95; both 13.38% to the cent). The Clark County General Information Guide for Transient Lodging (July 2021 edition) lists per-property rows that include Wynn/Encore, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, MGM Grand, ARIA and Bally's at 13.38% (Primary Gaming Corridor), and its Appendix III chart prints 13.38% for a resort hotel in SD & PGC. Horseshoe is not listed under its own name; Bally's, at the same street address (3645 Las Vegas Blvd S), appears at 13.38%, but the former name is not treated as Horseshoe's own licence, so Horseshoe stays open. Only part of the guide was read (chunks 0 and 3-11 of 12); the rows for Wynn, Bellagio, MGM Grand and Venetian were not all read to their licence numbers and are not quoted here. The guide is dated July 2021; the county's guidance page lists an April 2021 rate table as 'Updated', and no 2026 rate table was found, so the listing must be re-confirmed. DECISION NEEDED: the taxRate column is blank by policy (tests enforce 'a figure the property printed'); the county figure is shown only as a reference beside it. Whether a government per-property listing may fill that column is a user decision (see suggestions). True nightly cost still needs a dated base rate from each property, which none of these six has published.

flags.title: Two official Venetian pages disagree on whether the resort fee is added to the rate or included in it
flags.detail: Partly resolved on 2026-11-17 by reading the resort-fee page itself, which the earlier pass had not quoted. The Venetian's own Resort Fee page states: 'Rates include a daily Resort Fee of $55 plus tax per night, payable upon check-in.' That page governs the fee and it supports the arithmetic this site uses: the poker-suite starting rates are quoted before the fee, the $55 is chargeable on top, and the floor is therefore ($119 + $55) x 1.1338 = $197.28 rather than a double-count. Two things stay open. First, the booking calendar footnote says the opposite - 'Pricing shown is best available suite and rate, includes daily resort fee, excludes taxes' - so one official page states the fee is added to the rate and another states it is already in it. Second, neither page says which convention the phone-only poker rate (EPOKR25) uses. The published floor keeps the conservative reading (fee added, +$55 a night, about $300 over seven nights); if the poker rate proves to be fee-inclusive, the true floor is about $154 a night, roughly $43 lower. Only a dated checkout total for the poker rate settles it. The same caution applies to the Horseshoe calendar cells, whose own page says they include the resort fee.

flags.title: The Horseshoe rate calendar printed two different grids five minutes apart on the same day
flags.detail: Both readings are kept in the rate log. At 01:26 UTC the December 2026 grid printed Dec 1 $449, Dec 4 $219, Dec 5 $369, Dec 6 $249, Dec 7 $229, Dec 8 $169, Dec 9 $149, Dec 10 $359, Dec 11 $479, Dec 12 $429, Dec 13 $56, Dec 18 $63, Dec 19 $219, Dec 25 $129, Dec 27 $149, Dec 30 $209 and Dec 31 $529. At 01:31 UTC the same page printed $379, $189, $313, $214, $198, $148, $132, $305, $404, $363, $55, $61, $189, $115, $132, $181 and $445 for the same dates. A flexible-month calendar cell is a moving observation, not a held price, and this site does not average or pick between them. Any trip budget built from these cells must be re-read on the day of booking. The Caesars Palace calendar, read the same way twice, returned no price cells at all. F47 records the same behaviour on the Venetian calendar; this flag is the Caesars-page instance, which matters because the Horseshoe cells are the only dated room rates any reviewed property publishes for the trip window.

flags.title: The official Wynn Signature Series structures file is a 'coming soon' placeholder, so 38 rows cannot be confirmed
flags.detail: Read on 2026-11-17. The URL the site cites for Wynn Signature Series structures (Wynn_Signature_Series_Structures.pdf) now returns only 'LAS VEGAS POKER / COMING SOON'. The series schedule PDF, read at the same time, prints the dates January 11-24, 2027 and tells guests to 'Scan the QR code for event structures'. There is therefore no readable official structure sheet for these 38 rows today, and their single-entry, re-entry and add-on status correctly stays 'not verified' rather than being inferred from the schedule. The schedule does print buy-in, guarantee, chips and level length for most rows, and those columns are shown. Re-read on 2026-11-19 by session arena/827185f7-poker3: the same URL still returns only 'LAS VEGAS / POKER / COMING SOON' (document title 'Poker Tournament - Details Coming Soon'), so the flag stands and the 38 rows stay unverified.

flags.title: Two of the seven planned nights (23 and 24 November) do not satisfy the published condition for the $119 poker-suite rate
flags.detail: Corrected 2026-11-17. The earlier text of this flag named 30 November, 1 December and 2 December, which belonged to the superseded 25 November - 2 December window and are not part of the booked stay; the finding is unchanged in substance and only the dates were wrong. Derived from two published documents, not inferred. The Venetian poker-suite rate page requires 'six hours of active live cash gameplay or buy in to a $300 or higher tournament for each night stayed', and failure to qualify means the prevailing rate is charged. The trip is 23-30 November 2026, so the seven nights that must qualify are 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28 and 29 November. The day plan places a $400, $300, $600, $600 and $300 primary on 25, 26, 27, 28 and 29 November, which satisfy it, and a $200 primary on 23 and 24 November, which do not; those two nights are therefore not covered by the published condition. The page does not say whether an entry counts on the day it is paid or on every night of a multi-day event, so no re-pricing amount is claimed - the room must be asked. One $300+ alternative is published on each of those two dates: the $400 No Limit Hold'em 1A at 11:10 AM on 23 November and 1B at 11:10 AM on 24 November, both multi-flight, so both sit outside the single-entry screen and would also require playing into a later day. Choosing between a $200 buy-in with a possibly repriced room, a $400 multi-flight entry, or six hours of live cash play is a decision this site shows but does not make.

flags.title: The build sandbox cannot reach the venue hosts; live reads were made by the page reader
flags.detail: Every official venue and property host refused or timed out from the build sandbox, so the fetches in this pass were made by the assistant's page reader one URL at a time. This is recorded so a reader understands why an automated checks run can report 'unreachable' for a URL that loads normally in a browser.

flags.title: The NYE schedule page prints the year 2025 on its December 26 rows
flags.detail: The official DeepStack Extravaganza NYE page is headed 'December 24, 2026 - January 10, 2027', but its three December 26 rows read 'Saturday, December 26, 2025'. December 26 is a Saturday in 2026 (not in 2025, when it was a Friday), so the weekday is right and the year is the typo. The rows are listed with the series dates and the printed year is flagged rather than corrected. All 15 NYE structure sheets have since been read (see F11), so the printed year is the only open point on these rows.

flags.title: The Caesars page gives a general session length, not an event finish time
flags.detail: The official Caesars Palace poker-tournament page says 'Most sessions finish in four to six hours.' That is a general statement about its tournaments, not a published finish time for any event. The six-hour planning assumption for every room therefore remains an assumption.

flags.title: Two NYE events share one 11:10 AM start on January 4, 2027
flags.detail: The official DeepStack Extravaganza NYE schedule page lists Event #20 ($1,600 MSPT Day 2 Restart) and Event #27 ($250 No Limit Hold'em 1A $75K GTD) at 11:10 AM on the same day. Every other Day 2 or Day 3 restart row in both Venetian series is published at 10:00, 11:00 AM or 12:00 PM, never at 11:10 AM, while every 1A/1B/1C starting flight is published at 11:10 AM or 5:10 PM. The restart time therefore looks like a transcription slip on the official page rather than a genuine 11:10 AM restart, but this cannot be settled from the repository's copy, so the row is published exactly as the official page has it and is not adjusted. Confirm against the official page before sequencing anything on that date.

flags.title: Resumption rows carry no late-registration cut-off and no estimated finish
flags.detail: 45 rows are resumptions of a field that closed on an earlier day: Day 2, Day 3, Day 4 and Day 5 restarts and streamed final tables at the Venetian and at Wynn. Earlier in this build those rows printed the structure sheet's late-registration clause and the session length derived from it, but both belong to the earlier day's flight, not to the restart: registration closed when that day ended, and no venue publishes a restart finish time. On the LIPS streamed final table this produced a 7:00 PM start with a 'late registration until 4:55 PM' that closed three hours earlier, and an estimated finish at 6:30 PM the following afternoon. Both fields are now blank on those rows, with the reason recorded on the row. Four NYE rows that had been misclassified as restarts were also corrected: '$250 No Limit Hold'em 1A/1B/1C/1D $75K GTD - Day 1 payouts with 5% advancing to Day 2' are starting flights, not resumptions, because their 'Day 2' mention sits in the trailing payout clause. Continuation detection is now one shared rule instead of four separate regexes, two of which could not see a bare 'Final Table' row.

flags.title: Three NYE sheets print one late-registration clause covering two start times
flags.detail: Sheets dse_dec_2026-structure_4, _5 and _15 print a single late-registration clause with two clock times, for example '6 levels + break (~5:25 PM or ~8:25 PM)', because one sheet covers more than one start flight. The builder previously took the first clock time on every row, which put a 5:25 PM cut-off on the 6:10 PM row and closed registration before that event began. The row now takes the earliest printed time that still falls after its own start, so the 3:10 PM row keeps 5:25 PM and the 6:10 PM row takes 8:25 PM. Both times are printed on the sheet, so this disambiguates published values rather than inventing one; where no printed time falls after a row's start, no cut-off is published at all. Sheet _5 prints '5:25 PM or 12:25 PM' and no row in this schedule would take the 12:25 PM figure, so confirm the 12:25 PM reading with the poker room.

flags.title: The Bellagio Saturday structure sheet prints a blind level as 200-4300
flags.detail: The sheet linked from the Bellagio poker-room page prints the third blind level of the Saturday event as '200-4300', which does not fit the level ladder used by the neighbouring levels. Re-read 2026-11-17; the value is reported exactly as printed and no level data is derived from it.

flags.title: NYE structure_14 header names only Day 1B & 1D although three flights link to it
flags.detail: The official NYE schedule links the 5:10 PM flights on January 7, 8 and 9, 2027 (Day 1B, 1D and 1F) to dse_dec_2026-structure_14.pdf, but the sheet's flight header prints 'Day 1B & 1D @ 5:10 PM with Day 2 @ 12:00 PM' without Day 1F. The structure_14 rules are applied to all three linked rows and the header mismatch is flagged here. Read 2026-11-17.

flags.title: 30 November and 1 December 2026 print no figure in any reading, so a stay spanning them cannot be booked online
flags.detail: The official Venetian booking calendar was read on 2026-11-17 with two different stay windows open. Every date in the captured range printed a figure in at least one of the two renderings except two: 30 November and 1 December were blank in both. An arrival date of 30 November returns the message “We're sorry, but there is no availability for some of your selected dates. Please select different dates to proceed.” No rate, no suite and no checkout total can therefore be obtained online for a stay that includes either night. This is why the recommended trip is 23 November to 30 November and not 25 November to 2 December: the longer window spans two nights the engine will not price, so it cannot be booked as one stay. This finding does not depend on treating a calendar cell as a price — F47 records that the cells move with the query, and F28 that they disagree with the quote. It is narrower than either: across two independent renderings these were the only two dates that printed no figure at all. Confirm by phone on 866.255.8936 before booking either night.

flags.title: NYE Event #29 CES-badge discount is $10 on the schedule page but $20 on the structure sheet
flags.detail: The official DeepStack Extravaganza NYE schedule row for Event #29 (Jan 6, 2027, 5:10 PM) prints 'Show Your CES Badge - $10 RAKE DISCOUNT', but the event's structure sheet (dse_dec_2026-structure_2.pdf) prints: 'any player who shows their CES badge at the time of registration will receive a $20 discount on house fees for a total buy in of $180 instead of $200'. Both are official; neither was adjusted. Confirm the discount with the poker room before relying on it.

flags.title: MSPT (Event #20) Day 2 restart is 11:10 AM on the schedule page but 11:00 AM on the structure sheet
flags.detail: The official NYE schedule prints the Event #20 Day 2 Restart on Jan 4, 2027 at 11:10 AM, while the event's structure sheet (dse_dec_2026-structure_8.pdf) prints 'Day A+B+C @ 11:10 AM with Day 2 @ 11:00 AM'. The stored row keeps the schedule time (11:10 AM) and the sheet excerpt is recorded on the row's rules. F48 flags the same restart time from a different angle (two events share the 11:10 AM slot); the sheet evidence here shows the printed restart is 11:00 AM. Confirm the restart time with the poker room.

flags.title: MGM Grand's official poker page and its official weekly schedule PDF print different start times
flags.detail: Both pages were re-read on 2026-11-17. The poker-room page states 'Daily Texas Hold'em Tournaments 11:00am, 7:00pm and 11:00pm'. The weekly schedule PDF linked from that same page prints 11:10am, 7:10pm and 11:10pm on all seven days. The published rows follow the PDF. The difference is ten minutes, so it cannot change whether an event is reachable, but a player who arrives on the strength of the HTML time would miss the first ten minutes. flags.title: MGM Grand's only printed entry-policy statement for the $120 daily assumes five or more entries

flags.title: On five of the seven trip days the published fallback was the same event the site publishes as an impossible sequence against that day's primary (found and fixed 2026-11-19)
flags.detail: Found on 2026-11-19 by comparing site/data.json against its own stated fallback rule. The rule said the fallback 'starts after the primary's estimated finish plus a 30-minute transfer', but the builder selected the next-ranked candidate without applying that test. On 25, 26, 27, 28 and 29 November 2026 the fallback therefore started inside the primary's estimated session, and the same pair also appeared under planConflicts as an 'impossible sequence' on the schedule page. One block said the pair cannot be played; the other offered it as the plan. No official value was wrong and no tournament, fee, guarantee, hotel or walking figure changed. The fix adds an explicit sequence status to every fallback: 'replaces the primary' where it starts before the primary's estimated finish plus the transfer, and 'playable after the primary' where it starts later, each with a plain-language note on the schedule page. The stated rule now matches the code, and tests/test_fallback_sequencing.py fails if any fallback is again described as playable after an event it overlaps. This does not resolve the underlying limit: no venue publishes finish times (F16), so the replaced-or-after judgement still rests on an estimate.

The MGM Grand cells are logged with the room type the page names in its own picker ('Price on calendar for MGM King'); the Bellagio cells are deliberately NOT logged as a Bellagio rate and its room rate stays blank. flags.title: The poker-room parking waiver the venue prints for players is now carried by both Venetian rows, with the paid fee left in every total
flags.detail: Found on 2026-11-17 by re-reading the official poker-room pages (22:31Z), and reached independently on the same day by the session that put the poker-room page on The Venetian row's citation. The finding is the asymmetry: the Wynn row has carried a poker-room parking benefit for some time, while the Venetian and Palazzo rows published only the paid self-parking figures. The resort's own page, https://www.venetianlasvegas.com/resort/casino/poker/player-parking.html, prints both the rates ('The daily fee for registered hotel guests is $20/day, seven days a week') and the waiver: 'Players in the poker room who play three hours or more in tournament or cash games will receive complimentary self-parking for the day. Players must visit a supervisor at the end of their session to confirm qualifications for complimentary self-parking.' What this session adds on top of the citation: The Palazzo row now states the same policy (cited to the same poker-room page, which prints both the guest rate and the waiver); both rows and the trip-cost model carry the waiver as a dated, structured field with the verbatim text, the supervisor condition, the Sapphire tier route and the reason it is not applied; the calculator prints the waiver beside its parking field; and Q12 answers the question from the venue's page. NO TOTAL WAS CHANGED. The paid $20 a night stays in the calculator and in every published trip total, because no official source publishes a tournament finish time (F16) so the three-hour condition cannot be confirmed from a schedule, the page requires a supervisor to confirm the session, and the same page warns 'Event parking rates may be in effect' and that rates are 'subject to change'. What the page does not say - whether the waiver reaches an overnight folio charge or only the exit gate - is left blank, not guessed. MGM Resorts' own parking pages (MGM Grand, ARIA, Bellagio) could not be reached from this environment on 2026-11-17, so those three parking cells stay empty rather than being filled from third-party write-ups; Caesars Palace and Horseshoe publish only "surcharge applies" with no figure on the pages read.
