questions.question: What nightly budget and quality floor apply?
questions.answer: Not supplied. No comparable official quality score exists for these rooms, so the site leaves the quality ranking blank rather than inventing one.
questions.blocking: Yes - it decides which properties are shortlisted
questions.how: Give a maximum true cost per night and the minimum standard you accept, then re-run the comparison with the published rate floors.

questions.question: Is one total entry per player actually required, or only one entry per event?
questions.answer: For 52 Venetian one-day candidates, the official sheets print one buy-in and no re-entry, rebuy, add-on or second-flight clause. They do not state a maximum number of entries per player or explicitly say 'single entry' or 'freezeout'. The site therefore calls these sheet-screened candidates only; written confirmation from the venue is still needed before treating them as eligible. Wynn, Bellagio, MGM Grand and Caesars rows with printed re-entry, rebuy or add-on clauses are isolated in the separate extra-spend section.
questions.blocking: Yes - the maximum-entry policy is not published in the reviewed sheets
questions.how: Ask the poker room to confirm in writing that a second buy-in is not accepted for a specific event if that matters for your decision.

questions.question: Which hotels actually publish a room price for the dates you want?
questions.answer: Only The Venetian, and only through its own booking engine rather than on the rate page. Re-read on 2026-11-17, the engine printed $621.75 + $55 and $164.25 + $55 with $119.89 tax and a $1,015.89 total for a 650 sq ft Luxury King suite on November 17-19, against $1,245.48 for the same stay the day before, plus $2,504.00 for November 20-22. For the trip window itself it returned no suite at all. The engine's calendar cells are not prices: read twice on the same day, November 16 printed $555 with one stay window open and $854 with another, and November 27 printed $905 against $1,814 (F47). The last sentence of this answer was superseded later on 2026-11-17: the engine DID price the trip window (23-30 Nov 2026, $4,010.55 checkout total, logged in the rate log) and, on a second read about 20 minutes later, a Palazzo Luxury King at $3,823.46 (F78). The rate page still publishes only starting rates of $119 and $209, which are explicitly not date-specific, and states that rates are provided up to 150 days out. Two other properties now have dated figures too, both from their own booking pages on 2026-11-17: MGM Grand printed MGM King calendar cells (22-28 Nov $84, $84, $84, $84, $149, $349, $149; 30 Nov $649) under a legend that says the cells include the average daily resort fee and exclude taxes, and Horseshoe printed its own November and December grids. A calendar cell is not a checkout total; only the Venetian has a printed, itemised checkout total for the trip stay.
questions.how: Open the booking link with the exact dates, then log the printed total in the rate log with its timestamp.

questions.question: Will the poker-suite rate be honoured if you play tournaments rather than cash games?
questions.answer: Yes, in writing: the rate page requires 'six hours of active live cash gameplay or buy in to a $300 or higher tournament for each night stayed', met before 2 a.m. on the last night. A $100 or $200 tournament does not qualify; a $300 or higher entry does.
questions.how: Plan at least one $300+ entry per night stayed, or accept the prevailing rate.

questions.question: How long do the tournaments actually run, so two events can be sequenced?
questions.answer: Not published. Sheets give start time, level length and the late-registration cut-off, but no finish time. The overlap check on this site uses a stated six-hour session assumption plus a 30-minute transfer, and labels every conflict as an estimate.
questions.blocking: No, but it limits the day plan
questions.how: Ask the poker room for expected finish times, or treat the plan as a template and confirm on the day.

questions.question: What is the real walking time between each hotel and each poker room?
questions.answer: The venues publish no walking times. On 2026-11-17 every hotel was read to the Venetian poker room in Google Maps walking mode (first route card): The Palazzo 4 minutes, Wynn 13, Bellagio 21, Caesars Palace 12, Horseshoe 16, MGM Grand 35 and ARIA 31 (ARIA's other shown routes run to 38). The Venetian itself is in-property. These are Google Maps measurements, not official venue times (F84). Other hotel-to-room pairs, and every pair that includes Mandalay Bay, are not checked (F32).
questions.blocking: Yes - hotel-to-room pairs other than the Venetian are not checked
questions.how: Use official property addresses to verify each hotel-to-room Google or Apple walking route; do not assume missing pairs are under 30 minutes.

questions.question: Which other Strip rooms should be added to the plan?
questions.answer: Mandalay Bay was added on 2026-11-17: its official page is open Wednesday to Monday but prints no tournament schedule (F85). Resorts World and Planet Hollywood are reported closed in press only (F79, F80; unverified) and are listed on the Strip-room status table, not as candidates. Not checked: South Point, Golden Nugget, Circa, Excalibur, Luxor, Orleans, Red Rock, Palms, Westgate, Tropicana, Bally's, Flamingo, LINQ, Rio and M Resort.
questions.how: Say which properties to add; each needs its own official page and structure sheets.

questions.question: Do the December 17-23 and holiday-week events still run as published?
questions.answer: Re-read on 2026-11-17. Venetian DeepStack Extravaganza IV (the page covers Nov 16 to Dec 23, 2026): the 21 rows dated Nov 16 to Nov 27 match the page on date, start time, event name, buy-in, guarantee and structure-sheet link. The 73 rows dated Nov 28 to Dec 23 match on date, start time, event name, buy-in and guarantee; their structure links were not compared. Caesars Palace (four daily starts at 10 AM, 2 PM, 6 PM and 9 PM, $100 buy-in, $1,000 guarantee) and Horseshoe (six daily starts from 9 AM to 11 PM) match the page text. The page gives no Horseshoe buy-in or guarantee, so those cells stay blank. The Venetian resort fee is still $55 plus tax. The Wynn landing page confirms the WPT window and the Super Gold Million terms. The Bellagio landing page still carries a stale notice (flag F03). Not re-read by the 2026-11-17 pass that produced this answer: the Bellagio weekly PDFs, the Wynn daily and WPT PDFs and the DeepStack NYE schedule. They were read by the sessions recorded on the sources page, and each row shows its own read and verified dates.
questions.how: Re-check the Flagged for review page and the change log before booking and again 48 hours before you travel.

questions.question: What is the cancellation deadline at each property?
questions.answer: Published and different, all re-read live on 2026-11-17. Wynn: 'cancellations must be received at least 48 hours prior to arrival date or deposit (if applicable) will be forfeited', plus an early-departure penalty, with offer-specific date exceptions on the same page (F35 corrected). Bellagio, MGM Grand and ARIA: the first night's deposit is refundable if Room Reservations receives notice at least 72 hours before arrival; later cancellations and no-shows forfeit it. Caesars Palace and Horseshoe: the property pages advertise 'FREE 48-Hour Cancellation*' but do not print the terms behind the asterisk. Venetian: a deposit is billed on confirmation, blackout dates apply, prepaid offers are non-refundable, and an early checkout costs $100 plus tax.
questions.how: Use the cancellation column in the hotel table when choosing where to hold the booking.

questions.question: What does parking cost, and does it change the true cost per night?
questions.answer: Venetian: $20 per day for registered hotel guests, $20 Monday-Thursday and $25 Friday-Sunday for non-hotel guests, valet $40. The poker room's own parking page adds a waiver the hotel terms page does not print: players who play three hours or more in tournament or cash games receive complimentary self-parking for that day, confirmed with a supervisor at the end of the session (re-read 2026-11-17). A registered guest staying on property and playing a six-hour session therefore may pay nothing for parking, which is why the trip calculator keeps parking out of the core formula and shows it separately. Wynn: self-parking is free for registered guests and $25 per day for others, valet $40, and complimentary self-parking extends to Wynn poker-room guests. Bellagio, MGM Grand and ARIA publish no parking figure on their reservation terms pages, so those cells stay blank rather than guessed.
questions.how: Parking stays in the trip total at $20 a night. If the room confirms three or more hours of play for a day, that night's self-parking is complimentary per the page, so set the parking field to 0 for those days rather than assuming the waiver in advance.

questions.question: Are you 21 or older with a Venetian Rewards card, and are you 50 or older for the Seniors events?
questions.answer: Each of the seven DeepStack Extravaganza IV sheets re-read on 2026-11-17 requires players to be 21+ and to hold a Venetian Rewards card. The Dec 2 10:10 AM $600 No Limit Hold'em Seniors event (#24) is open only to players 50 or older. Sheet 17, read on 2026-11-16 and re-read line by line on 2026-11-17, prints 'MUST BE 50+ YEARS OF AGE TO PARTICIPATE' and adds that a player who buys in under 50 is not entitled to prize money or a refund of the buy-in, so the age limit is confirmed on the sheet and not only on the schedule. The day plan leaves age-restricted events out, so the Dec 2 primary stays the 5:10 PM bounty and this Seniors event is listed only as an alternative for a player who is 50+.
questions.blocking: Yes - eligibility decides which of the trip-window events a player can enter
questions.how: Confirm your age band and whether you hold a Venetian Rewards card. If you are 50+, the Dec 2 Seniors event (#24) is open to you: its sheet is read and its fee, guarantee, chips and late-registration cut-off are on the row.

questions.question: Does the 8 AM start the brief asks for exist anywhere on the Strip?
questions.answer: Not on any official source read for this build. The earliest verified start is Horseshoe's daily game at 9:00 AM on the Caesars page (read 2026-11-17), which publishes no buy-in or structure. Caesars Palace starts at 10:00 AM. The earliest Venetian start is 9:10 AM (a satellite on Dec 12), and the earliest non-satellite Venetian start is 10:10 AM. An all-day 8 AM plan therefore cannot be built from verified data; the day plan starts at the first verified open event for each venue. For the trip window itself (23-29 November) no opening event starts before 11:10 AM; the only earlier start there is a Day 2 restart at 11:00 AM on 25 November (F17, read 2026-11-19).
questions.blocking: Yes - the all-day schedule in the brief cannot be produced without it
questions.how: Ask Horseshoe for the buy-in, structure and single-entry rule of its 9:00 AM game; ask each room for its earliest daily start.

questions.question: What is the real checkout total for the trip dates?
questions.answer: Partly answered 2026-11-17. The official Venetian booking engine printed an itemised checkout total of $4,010.55 for 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-30 (two adults, Luxury King suite, best available rate; $55 resort fee each night and $473.30 tax). Earlier readings for 2026-11-25 to 2026-12-02 showed the placeholder '$XXX' in every calendar cell and no total (F57). Re-read 2026-11-19: the same booking link still showed only a loading page with no total, so the $4,010.55 figure is not a price for today (F93). No other property publishes a date-specific total in the data. The phone-only poker rate is not in the quote (F66).
questions.blocking: Yes - the engine total is now known, but the poker-rate total the budget is built on is not
questions.how: Open the booking engine in a browser, select the dates and two adults, and read the checkout total; or call the poker rate line on 866.255.8936 and ask for code EPOKR25 priced for those dates.

questions.question: Do the poker hotel rates require play that the trip plan actually satisfies?
questions.answer: Yes, and it changes the risk. The Venetian poker rate requires six hours of active live cash play, or a buy-in to a $300 or higher tournament, for each night stayed. Any night that misses the requirement is repriced at the prevailing rate at checkout. Measured against the published plan on 2026-11-17: five of the seven nights carry a $300 or higher primary (Nov 25 $400, Nov 26 $300, Nov 27 $600, Nov 28 $600, Nov 29 $300) and two do not (Nov 23 and Nov 24, both $200). The seven nights are 23-29 November because the trip ends with an 11:00 a.m. check-out on 30 November, which is a departure day and not a night. Each day of the plan prints its own result. What the page does not say is whether one entry covers every night of a multi-day event, or only the night it is paid - ask the room before treating the $119 floor as certain (F54).
questions.blocking: No, but it decides which events belong on which day
questions.how: Confirm with the poker room that the tournament buy-in counts on the day it is paid, and whether a Day 2 return counts again.

questions.question: Which hotel fees are still unverified, and does that break the comparison?
questions.answer: Corrected 2026-11-17: every one of the eight properties now has a verified resort fee. Caesars Palace prints $54.95 plus $7.35 tax ($62.30 tax inclusive) and Horseshoe $49.95 plus $6.68 ($56.63), both on their own booking pages; MGM Grand $50, Bellagio $55, ARIA $55, Wynn $55 and the Venetian $55 come from each property's own reservation terms. What remains unverified is the ROOM-TAX PERCENTAGE: only the Venetian prints 13.38%, so true-nightly figures stay blank at the other properties and the comparison is incomplete rather than wrong (F39). The site leaves those cells blank and flags them.
questions.blocking: No - the recommended property is fully verified
questions.how: Read each property's own reservation terms page, or ask the front desk for the resort fee and tax in writing.

questions.question: What happens if a scheduled re-check reports a changed page?
questions.answer: Nothing changes automatically. scripts/verify_transcription.py stores a SHA-256 of each page and flags a change; a person then re-reads the source before any value moves. This is deliberate: a venue can change a guarantee, a fee or a start time without notice, and an automatic overwrite would publish an unread number as if it had been verified.
questions.blocking: No - it is a process question
questions.how: Watch the Sources page; a changed URL is listed with its previous and current hash.

suggestions.title: Publish a nightly rate snapshot per property and week
suggestions.detail: Rooms are priced per night and the published rates are only available up to 150 days out. A weekly snapshot of the official starting rate, the mandatory resort fee and the tax for each property would turn a blank column into a comparable one and would let the rate log show movement.
suggestions.decision: Needs a data source that the venue publishes without login

suggestions.title: Add a per-venue finish-time estimate that the poker room confirms
suggestions.detail: The overlap check is the weakest part of the plan because no venue publishes a finish time. A simple field on each structure sheet, confirmed by the room, would make the day plan exact instead of assumed.
suggestions.decision: Ask each poker room; the Venetian publishes structure sheets it controls

suggestions.title: Read the remaining WPT event sections and the rest of the Strip schedule
suggestions.detail: Closed for the WPT structures: the official structures PDF was read in full (all eight chunks) on 2026-11-17 and every event section it publishes is transcribed in raw/wynn_wpt_world_championship_structures_2026-11-17.md, with 35 rows now quoting their own section (F12, F77). Reading it did NOT move any event into the single-entry filter, because every section prints re-entry. Still open, and now precisely bounded: the $10,400 WPT World Championship, the Dec 18 high-roller and $3,000 events, the Super Gold Million Mystery Bounty, the Seniors and Ladies championships, the NLH Mystery Bounty, the Wynn Mixed Championship, the TORSE and Limit Omaha 8 championships and every Milestone Satellite have no published section at all, so no amount of reading this document settles them. 101 WPT rows stay unverified for that reason. The next step is to ask the Wynn poker room for those sheets or to watch the same URL for a re-issue.
suggestions.decision: Ask the Wynn poker room for the unpublished sections; no new source to find

suggestions.title: Add the missing Strip poker rooms
suggestions.detail: Mandalay Bay was added on 2026-11-17 (F85). Resorts World and Planet Hollywood are reported closed in press only (F79, F80; unverified). South Point, Golden Nugget, Circa, Excalibur, Luxor, Orleans, Red Rock, Palms, Westgate, Tropicana, Bally's, Flamingo, LINQ, Rio and M Resort are all unverified. For a trip that aims to enter as many tournaments as possible, the daily rooms in walking range are worth more than another marquee series.
suggestions.decision: Which properties to prioritise

suggestions.title: Replace the estimated walking times with a venue-published figure
suggestions.detail: No venue publishes a walking time. Asking each property for the official route and time to its own poker room would replace Google Maps estimates, which are model outputs that ignore indoor walkways and Strip traffic. Until then the site only filters on measured pairs: as of 2026-11-17 the tournaments table's 30-minute limit is opt-in, is measured from the hotel the reader selects, labels a figure used in the reverse of its recorded direction, and counts the rows it hides as either over the limit or unmeasured.
suggestions.decision: Worth doing for the final shortlist

suggestions.title: Capture the hotel cost components for the remaining properties
suggestions.detail: STATUS UPDATED 2026-11-17. The fee half of this is closed: all eight properties now carry a resort fee taken from the property's own page (Venetian, Palazzo, Wynn and Bellagio $55, MGM Grand $50, Caesars Palace $54.95, Horseshoe $49.95, ARIA $55), and Caesars Palace and Horseshoe additionally print the tax on that fee, which divides to 13.376% and 13.373% and corroborates the 13.38% the model applies. What still blocks a like-for-like ranking is the room rate: no property except the Venetian publishes a dated price a static reader can reach, so true cost per night exists only for the Venetian and the Palazzo. Parking is published for Venetian, Palazzo, Wynn, Caesars and Horseshoe and not for MGM Grand, Bellagio or ARIA.
suggestions.decision: Straightforward research, no new source needed

suggestions.title: Add a bankroll-versus-prize view that states the assumption
suggestions.detail: The site deliberately shows guaranteed pool divided by entry fee as a descriptive ratio and never as a forecast. A clearly labelled scenario panel could show how many buy-ins a fixed bankroll buys against a given guarantee, with the assumption written next to the number.
suggestions.decision: Whether to include any modelling at all

suggestions.title: Add a seat-availability check for the recommended day plan
suggestions.detail: The Venetian requires a Venetian Rewards card to play and the Wynn requires Wynn Rewards membership. A pre-trip checklist for rewards enrolment, and a note about MGM Rewards for Bellagio and MGM Grand, would remove a common day-of-trip failure.
suggestions.decision: Straightforward content addition

suggestions.title: Let the planner remember a trip profile
suggestions.detail: Dates, nightly budget, party size and the single-entry rule are the same four inputs on every page. Storing them in the browser would let the date filter, the hotel comparison and the cost calculator agree with each other.
suggestions.decision: Local storage only, no account

suggestions.title: Publish the change-detection log as a first-class page
suggestions.detail: The scheduled checker already records a dated status and content hash for every official URL. Surfacing it on its own page, with the rows that changed highlighted on the tournament tables, is what turns the site from a snapshot into something you can trust on the morning you travel.
suggestions.decision: Already implemented in this pass - confirm the presentation

suggestions.title: Resolve the Bellagio Saturday buy-in conflict with the poker room
suggestions.detail: Three official sources print three different buy-ins for the same event. A single written answer from the room would let the event be ranked instead of being left blank.
suggestions.decision: Send the conflict list to the room

suggestions.title: Retire the four superseded dashboards
suggestions.detail: The repository still holds five dashboards from earlier parallel sessions (root pages, docs/, verified/, planner/, single-entry/). Only site/ is published by the Pages workflow, so the others are audit artefacts. Removing or archiving them would stop them diverging from the live data.
suggestions.decision: Keep as archive or delete

suggestions.title: Settle the missing facts before any booking decision
suggestions.detail: Six things are known and seven are not, and the difference decides the trip. Known from official sources: every DeepStack IV and NYE structure sheet, every printed buy-in and fee, the Venetian resort fee and 13.38% room tax, the Venetian $20 guest parking, and the cancellation rules for the Venetian, Bellagio, MGM Grand, ARIA and Wynn. Not known: the real checkout total for the trip dates, the Wynn and Caesars tax percentages, the Caesars and Horseshoe resort fees, any published tournament finish time, the WPT event-level re-entry rules, whether the poker rate's play requirement counts a tournament buy-in on the day it is paid, and whether any room opens before 09:10 AM. Each one has a question card on the Questions page.
suggestions.decision: Answer the blocking questions on the Questions page, in the order they are listed

suggestions.title: Price the same seven-night stay in a browser, then log it
suggestions.detail: The booking engine renders its prices with script, so the three sources that can read a checkout total are a real browser, the poker-rate phone line (866.255.8936, code EPOKR25) or the front desk. Whichever answers, record the arrival date, departure date, occupancy, room type, nightly rate, resort fee, tax, total and the timestamp as one new dated rate-log entry. That single row would replace the $197.28 floor with a real number for the recommended dates.
suggestions.decision: One phone call or one browser session; no new source needed

suggestions.title: Ask the three rooms with unverified fees for the numbers in writing
suggestions.detail: Caesars Palace and Horseshoe publish room prices but no resort fee, and Wynn prints 'plus tax' without a percentage. A written fee schedule from each property would let all eight properties be compared like for like for the first time. Until then the comparison on the trip cost page shows those rows blank on purpose.
suggestions.decision: Send the same three-question request to each property

suggestions.title: Count the levels to the money instead of assuming one session length
suggestions.detail: The day plan estimates a finish from the late-registration cut-off plus two levels, which is honest but still an assumption. Every structure sheet prints the full blind schedule and the payout percentage, so the levels to the money could be counted to produce a field-size-based finish range. That would turn the overlap flags from estimates into arithmetic on published data.
suggestions.decision: Whether to publish a modelled finish range or keep one stated assumption

suggestions.title: Confirm the WPT event-level re-entry rule for the three events inside the trip window
suggestions.detail: Closed. The structures PDF was read in full and each of the three WPT rows inside the trip window that has a published section now quotes it verbatim: the $600 TORSE on Nov 27 ('Unlimited re-entry will be available until the start of level 9'), the $400 PLO on Nov 27 and the $600 Limit Omaha 8 on Nov 30 (both 'Unlimited re-entry will be available until the start of level 9'). All three are multi-entry, so none of them is a single-entry candidate. The 82 WPT rows still marked unverified are events the document does not cover, not rows this pass failed to read (F12).
suggestions.decision: No further action: the answer is that these events allow unlimited re-entry

suggestions.title: Re-quote the trip window every morning and log what the engine returns
suggestions.detail: Three dated quotes show the engine moves: the same November 17-19 stay printed $1,245.48 on 2026-11-16 and $1,015.89 on 2026-11-17. Four stay windows inside the trip window returned no suite at all. A scheduled job that opens the seven per-night booking links each morning and appends whatever the engine prints - a total, or 'no suite returned' - would turn the trip budget from a floor into a tracked number without anyone having to remember to look.
suggestions.decision: Automate the morning re-quote, or keep the per-night links manual

suggestions.title: Never treat a booking-calendar cell as a price
suggestions.detail: Read twice on the same day, the official calendar printed $555 and $854 for November 16 and $905 and $1,814 for November 27 depending on which stay window was open. The cell tracks the cheapest suite the engine can offer for that query, not a nightly rate. This is already enforced in the data - only the itemised quote panel is used - but the comparison is worth keeping on the hotels page so a reader does not copy a calendar figure into a budget.
suggestions.decision: Keep the comparison published - and since 2026-11-17 the calculator page itself warns against pasting a calendar cell into the room-rate box, quoting the two properties' own 'includes resort fee' sentences

suggestions.title: Ask the Venetian two questions in one call, then fix the rate basis once
suggestions.detail: Two open questions are answered by the same phone call to 866.255.8936 (code EPOKR25). (1) Is the $119 / $209 poker rate quoted before or after the $55 resort fee? The Resort Fee page says the fee is chargeable on top of the rate and the booking calendar says its prices include the fee, so the poker rate itself decides whether the $197.28 floor overstates the nightly cost by about $43 (F51). (2) Does one $300 or higher entry cover every night of a multi-day event, or only the night it is paid? The answer decides whether the 23 and 24 November nights are repriced (F54). A dated checkout total for the booked 23-30 November stay is already recorded ($4,010.55, F15), so quote the poker rate against that same stay to compare like for like.
suggestions.decision: One call settles the nightly budget basis, the qualification risk and the missing total

suggestions.title: Score each day on rate qualification as well as on guarantee
suggestions.detail: The day plan now prints, per day, whether the planned primary satisfies the published $300 condition for the poker-suite rate. Two ways to act on it: (a) leave 23 and 24 November as $200 primaries and budget those two nights at the prevailing rate, or (b) swap them for the published $400 No Limit Hold'em 1A / 1B at 11:10 AM on each day, which qualifies but moves both days out of the single-entry screen, because a flight shares a Day 2 with other flights. This site shows the trade-off and does not choose it, because it depends on whether the traveller values the verified rate or the single-entry format.
suggestions.decision: Add a 'qualifies for the poker rate' filter to the tournaments table (a $300+ buy-in filter on the same rows already published)

suggestions.title: Keep monitoring the two Caesars booking pages for a dated rate
suggestions.detail: The Caesars property booking pages publish a fee block and, for Horseshoe, a full dated month of lowest-available rates, in plain HTML rather than by script - unlike the Venetian engine, which prints $XXX. Both pages are now in the monitored source list, so the 12:10 UTC re-check will see a Caesars Palace calendar appear as soon as the property starts publishing one, and the rate log will keep both readings when a cell moves (F55). No scraper is needed for these two properties.
suggestions.decision: No further work: the URLs are in site/data.json sources and are re-checked on schedule

trip.checkoutNote: Check-out is 11:00 a.m. on 2026-11-30, so 30 November is a departure day, not a playable day. The seven playable days are 23-29 November 2026. The Venetian does publish a 5:10 p.m. $200 bounty on 30 November, but it cannot be played after an 11:00 a.m. check-out unless the player pays for a late check-out, which the official terms say is subject to an additional fee.
trip.nightlyBudgetNote: Two figures, because they answer different questions. The floor is $197.28: ($119 published poker-suite starting rate + $55 mandatory resort fee) x 1.1338 Clark County room tax. It is a floor computed from published components, not a quote. The $119 rate is available only by phone under code EPOKR25 and only to a player who meets the daily play requirement (F66). The dated figure is $572.94 a night all-in: the official Venetian booking engine's checkout total of $4,010.55 for 23-30 November 2026 (2 adults, Luxury King, read 2026-11-17 after 21:54 UTC), divided by seven nights. That total already includes the $55 resort fee and the 13.38% tax.
trip.qualityFloor: Fixed by this session on an objective published-evidence test rather than an invented score: the property must publish its own poker-room rate, keep the poker room on site, and publish its resort fee, tax and cancellation terms. No comparable official quality score exists for these rooms, so the quality column stays blank (F19).
rationale: 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-30 (7 nights, 7 playable days - 30 November is an 11 a.m. checkout day) holds 12 sheet-screened candidates whose sheets omit extra-entry terms, at least one on each playable date. This is not proof of a one-entry-per-player cap. The window moved here from 25 November - 2 December because the official booking engine will not price a stay spanning 30 November and 1 December (F57).

All 37 DeepStack Extravaganza IV structure sheets were read directly on 2026-11-16. The sheets are primary-source evidence for their printed terms, but they do not confirm a maximum number of entries per player; see F31.

The window stays inside DSE IV, the series whose 37 structure sheets were read first. The December 24, 2026 to January 10, 2027 DeepStack NYE series is fully published and all 15 of its sheets have been read; three of them print multi-entry wording, so those rows stay off the candidate list, and the whole series sits outside the trip window in any case (F11).
It also sits before the $10,400 WPT World Championship buy-in tier on December 13, which would break the trip budget on a single entry.
The Wynn WPT schedule runs from November 27 inside the window, so three days carry additional published rows, all clearly marked as series rows with unverified entry rules (F12).
trip.nightlyRisk: The night of Friday 27 November 2026, the night after Thanksgiving, is quoted at $1,649.25 room rate + $55 resort fee + tax = $1,932.28 all-in, against $248.59 all-in on 23 and 24 November. It is 48% of the whole $4,010.55 stay on its own. A player who can move the trip, or who is willing to change property for that one night, removes $1,683.69 of all-in cost compared with a $248.59 night. The phone-only poker rate ($119-$209 + $55) is the other lever, if the daily play requirement is met and the code applies to these dates (F66).
trip.bankrollNote: The 7 recommended primary entries total $2,600 in buy-ins. With a 25% buffer for one rebuy or an add-on where a room allows it, plan on $3,250. It is a planning number, not a forecast.
trip.lodgingEvidence: The official Venetian booking engine was opened on 2026-11-17 for several stay windows, with two adults. Four windows inside the originally considered 25 November - 2 December dates returned no suite or price: the seven-night stay and the November 30 single night rendered every calendar cell as the placeholder '$XXX', the November 25-27 stay did not finish loading, and the November 27-28 stay rendered the calendar with no suite panel. A further read the same day rendered 25 November through 1 December as 'Date Unavailable' (F57). The trip was therefore moved to 23-30 November, the seven-night window the engine prices on every night. A read on 2026-11-17 after 21:54 UTC priced that window in full: a checkout total of $4,010.55, with the nightly rate, the $55 resort fee and 13.38% tax itemised for each night. Those figures are the dated quote in the rate log and the basis of the observed nightly figure. The earlier $2,140 and $346.62 figures were the sum and average of calendar cells for the superseded window; the engine's own footnote says the cells are not the price, so they are withdrawn from the trip budget (F69). The engine quotes near-term stays too, and it priced the same 17-19 November stay twice on consecutive days ($1,245.48 on 2026-11-16 and $1,015.89 on 2026-11-17), so every figure here is dated and can move.
trip.pokerRateQualification: The Venetian poker-suite rate is held only if, for each night stayed, the player completes six hours of active live cash play or buys in to a $300 or higher tournament, before 2 a.m. on the last night. The recommended entries already meet the tournament test on 5 of the 7 nights: 2026-11-25 ($400), 2026-11-26 ($300), 2026-11-27 ($600), 2026-11-28 ($600), 2026-11-29 ($300). They do not meet it on 2026-11-23 ($200), 2026-11-24 ($200), where the primary event is under $300, so those nights depend on the six-hour cash-play test or on paying the prevailing rate. For every night the requirement is missed the rate is adjusted to the prevailing rate, which the booking calendar prices at $165 to $905 across these dates.

planNotes.primaryRule: Provisional primary candidate = the sheet-screened event on that date with the largest published guarantee, among venues within a 30-minute walk of the recommended hotel, excluding age-restricted, female-only and team formats. This is not confirmation of a one-entry-per-player cap; written venue rules are required.
planNotes.fallbackRule: Fallback = the next sheet-screened candidate on the same date, ranked after the primary, chosen as an alternative to it and never in addition to it. Where the fallback starts before the primary's estimated finish plus a 30-minute transfer, it is marked 'replaces the primary' and the same pair also appears under the impossible-sequence flags; it can only be played if the player is out of the primary in time to register. Where it starts later, it is marked 'playable after the primary'. The fallback is conditional on written confirmation of entry rules and fit.
planNotes.pokerRateRule: The hotel rate the budget is built on is conditional. Each night stayed needs either six hours of active live cash play or a $300 or higher tournament buy-in, per the official poker-suite rate page. Every day of the plan now carries a 'poker-rate condition' result against that rule; a night marked as not satisfying it may be repriced at the prevailing rate at checkout (F54).

parkingWaiver.excerpt: Players in the poker room who play three hours or more in tournament or cash games will receive complimentary self-parking for the day. Players must visit a supervisor at the end of their session to confirm qualifications for complimentary self-parking.
parkingWaiver.note: The $20 per night parking line above is the registered-guest self-parking fee. The resort's own poker-room parking page prints a waiver of it for players who play three hours or more, confirmed by a supervisor at the end of the session. The waiver is not netted off this total: no official source publishes a finish time for any event (F16), so the three-hour condition cannot be confirmed from a schedule, and a rate the venue reserves the right to change is not a saving to bank. Set the parking field to 0 in the calculator only once the room has confirmed it for you.

tripCostModel.cancellation: A deposit covering suite, fee and tax is billed on confirmation. Prepaid offers are non-cancellable and non-refundable. Early checkout costs $100 plus tax. No date-specific cancellation deadline was published for a flexible booking on the reviewed pages.
tripCostModel.note: Computed from the published starting rate, the published $55 resort fee and the published 13.38% Clark County room tax. It is a floor for the property, not a quote for any date. The official booking engine quoted a dated checkout total for the 23-30 Nov 2026 trip window on 2026-11-17; that quote is in liveQuote and is not this floor. The parking line is the registered-guest fee; the venue publishes a conditional waiver of it for players (see parkingWaiver), which is not netted off.

liveQuote.basis: Dated official booking-engine checkout total for two adults in a Luxury King suite, read 2026-11-17 after 21:54 UTC. It is the engine's best available rate, not the phone-only poker rate (F66), and it is one read, not a guarantee.

perNight.property: The Venetian Resort - venetian Newly Remodeled Luxury King suite
perNight.note: Re-read live from the official Venetian booking engine on 2026-11-17 for the exact trip window (2 adults, 7 nights). The per-night true costs are derived as (rate + $55) x 1.1338 and sum to the printed total. The engine's own 'Average Rate' line prints $505.32, which equals the average of (rate + $55 resort fee), confirming that its average-rate figure includes the resort fee. Printed tax is $0.02 above 13.38% of the printed pre-tax subtotal; the page does not explain the difference and the printed figures are kept as printed (flag F65). This is a dated observation, not a booking price: the engine's rates move between reads, and the poker-suite rate page adds a play-qualification condition and the EPOKR25 code.
